verdict.line: You lose if you walk into his 1100-range Q and trade autos while his E (Hop) is up; you win if you dash in with your E the instant his Hop goes on cooldown and chain into a stun before he can reset the gap.

brief.thesis: Gnar has no reliable way to create distance once his E (Hop, cooldown 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s) is down, and Renekton gets a 450-range gap closer in E (Slice and Dice) from level 2 onward. The matchup is a race between Renekton's Fury-fueled all-ins during Hop's cooldown window and Gnar's attempt to poke safely with Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) and kite away whenever Hop is up.

tell.watch: Gnar's Rage meter and E cooldown

theirWindow.when: his E (Hop) is up and your E is down
theirWindow.what: He'll poke freely with Q (1100 range) and harass with Hyper-empowered autos while kiting. Don't walk up to trade here — you'll eat ranged damage with no way to close before he hops away.

yourWindow.what: Immediately close with E (Slice and Dice, 450-range dash) and chain into W (Ruthless Predator) for the stun. He has no displacement until Hop refreshes, so this is your commit window — especially once you're above 50 Fury for the upgraded empowered Q and three-hit W.

start.why: The block-and-regen passive soaks the chip damage from his Q and Hyper-empowered autos while you walk up to threaten a trade, letting you arrive at range with more HP than a Doran's Blade start (48% WR, 63.4% pick).

boots.why: Gnar's entire poke package — Q, autos, Hyper bonus damage — is physical; Steelcaps (47.9% WR, 88% pick) directly reduces every hit he lands on you while you close in.

core.why: The proc shield absorbs a chunk of his Q poke or Hyper auto right as you commit your all-in during a Hop-down window.
Stacking armor shred keeps your empowered E and R damage relevant into his HP-stacked Mega Gnar form.
The bonus health and tenacy-adjacent survivability (50% WR over 108 games) let you tank through a stray W Wallop stun or R knockback without instantly dying to the follow-up.

situational.when: the game extends past 20-25 minutes and you need sustained damage mitigation instead of a single burst window (47.2% WR line)
their jungler or mid adds extra hard CC on top of Gnar's stuns
you want a mobility rush into Black Cleaver and Sterak's instead of Eclipse (55.4% WR over a smaller 56-game sample)

runes.keystoneWhy: Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing offsets Gnar's ranged poke damage while you close distance, and the stacks keep building through the extended skirmishes your Fury-based all-ins create (46.3% WR, highest-pick page in the data).

summoners.why: Given your lane and solo-kill advantage here, Ignite (48.2% WR, 68.2% pick) converts your level 2-5 all-in windows into kills before he can disengage, while Flash guarantees you can close the gap or extend a chase through terrain.

playing.title: Punish Hop cooldown
playing.detail: Track his E (Hop, 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s cooldown). The instant it's down, dash in with your E and chain into W for the stun — he has no way to create distance until it refreshes.

playing.title: Don't walk into Q range
playing.detail: His Q (1100 range) outranges your Q (325 range) by a wide margin. Hold just outside that range when his Hop is up so he can't poke you for free.

playing.title: Fury-check before committing
playing.detail: Check your Fury bar before diving. Above 50 Fury your W slashes three times for a 1.5s stun and destroys shields — wait the extra auto or two to cross that threshold before an all-in.

playing.title: Respect the Rage transform
playing.detail: Watch his Rage meter. At max Rage his next ability instantly triggers Mega Gnar, adding a ground-slam stun (W Wallop) and extra survivability mid-fight — don't start your stun chain right as his bar caps.

playing.title: Ult to tank the poke, not just for damage
playing.detail: Your R (Dominus) grants bonus health and periodic Fury generation alongside its initial damage pulse. Pop it when diving past level 6 to soak his Q poke and keep refilling Fury for a second empowered W.

playing.title: Post-6 pattern stays the same
playing.detail: His R (GNAR!) only fires once he's capped Rage and transformed — it doesn't replace Hop's short cooldown as his main disengage. Keep closing the instant Hop is down through the mid-game.

playing.title: Trade through Doran's Shield
playing.detail: The block-and-regen passive lets you walk up to his Q and Hyper-auto harassment with more HP banked than a straight damage start would give you.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, boots, summoners, and win rates above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (2,134 Renekton-vs-Gnar games at 48.7% win rate); the ability tells, timing windows, and trade-pattern reasoning are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep some distance to avoid being kited by Gnar while building up Fury. Close in to engage combat whenever Gnar’s (E) is on cooldown.
